answers.answer: 1. Each player starts with 25 money, one active worker on the notepad and three inactive workers lying on the reserve spaces. 2. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 as hidden hand cards and discard 4 face up. 3. Draw 2 hidden Final Scoring cards. 4. Place Animals in slot 1 (leftmost, strength 1), and randomly place the other four Action cards in the remaining slots; all begin side I up. 5. Appeal starts at 0 for the start player, then 1, 2 and 3 for second, third and fourth in turn order.

1. Put 3 face-up Base Conservation Projects below the Association board in 2- or 3-player games and 4 in a 4-player game. 2. In a 2-player game only, cover the left level on the left face-up project, middle level on the middle project, right level on the right project, and the three donation spaces in the donation area's left column; these spaces are blocked to both players. 3. In 3- and 4-player games none of those project levels or donation spaces is blocked at setup. 4. Reveal the six-card display only after everyone has selected their initial hand cards.

1. After using the card in slot 4, remove it; shift the cards that were in slots 1–3 one slot right, then put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set action strength before doing the action; each X-token spent beforehand adds 1 strength, with any number spendable subject to the five-token holding limit. Tokens gained during the action cannot boost that same action. 3. After-finishing effects resolve only after the action is complete, including moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: taking a turn; X-tokens; ‘After finishing’ effects

answers.answer: 1. You may not take a regular action that does nothing; for example, playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not legal. 2. Instead you may select an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token; its slot strength and upgrade side do not matter. 3. Move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards as usual. 4. You cannot take this alternative if you already have 5 X-tokens.

1. When the Break token reaches the last track space, ignore any additional steps beyond the end and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. 2. Finish the triggering player's current turn; the break occurs afterward. 3. After the break, return the token to the starting space for the player count and continue clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: The Break track; Break trigger from effects

answers.answer: 1. Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then choose either draw from the deck using the side-I strength table (up to 3 cards, with the indicated discard) or snap exactly 1 display card of your choice at strength 5 or more; snapping has no reputation restriction and replaces deck draw. 2. Cards II also advances the Break token 2 spaces, then draw from the deck and/or from the display within reputation range, in any order, using the side-II table. Its snap option is available at strength 3 or more and takes exactly 1 display card of any reputation, without a deck draw; the reputation restriction applies to display draws, not snapping. 3. Display cards are replenished at end of turn, not during the action. 4. There is no hand limit during a turn; discard to the limit at breaks.
answers.evidence: CARDS action; Special Rules: Display timing and Hand size

answers.answer: 1. Reputation range includes the display folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action (Cards II). 3. At reputation 15, further reputation does not move the counter; gain 1 appeal for each additional reputation step. 4. You may not inspect the discard pile during the game.

1. Build I builds exactly 1 building of size no greater than strength; Build II may build any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but not two identical buildings in the same action. 2. Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placement. 3. Your first building must include at least one map border space; later buildings must touch an existing building along an edge. 4. Build only on empty spaces, not beyond the map, overlapping, or covering water/rock; restricted-icon spaces require Build II. 5. Each kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 6. Each pavilion increases appeal by 1 immediately, once.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: building table, side I, placement rules, side II

answers.answer: 1. Build I can build standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo (size 3). Build II additionally permits the Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary, each size 5. 2. The supply has four tiles of each special enclosure type, but each zoo may have at most one Petting Zoo, one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary. 3. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. 4. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal; Build II allows access to restricted-icon spaces, though other effects can also complete coverage.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: Buildings available through Build; side I and side II

answers.answer: 1. Earlier gains during an action—including money, cards and newly activated workers—may be used for later steps of that same action; resolve items one at a time and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. 2. Thus a prior gain can fund a later building, animal or association task if it occurs before that later cost/task. 3. Ordinary immediate effects resolve as triggered; after-finishing effects wait until the whole action is done (and Action cards have moved). 4. When effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: X-tokens: resolve its items one at a time; Animals action; shared principles

answers.answer: 1. For each animal, meet every card condition, pay its printed cost, and provide legal housing; a partner zoo matching the animal's continent discounts cost by 3 money per continent icon printed on that animal, so a double continent icon discounts 6. 2. A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the animal's required size; house one animal and flip the whole enclosure to its occupied side. Petting Zoo animals can only go in the Petting Zoo. Eligible reptiles and some birds may instead use a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, placing supply player tokens equal to the animal's indicated space requirement; special enclosures are never flipped and must have that many free spaces. 3. The chosen housing, including a special enclosure, must meet the animal's water/rock adjacency needs; count distinct adjacent hexes. 4. Resolve ordinary effects after admitting each animal, before the next animal; after-finishing effects wait until the Animals action and Action-card movement are complete. For two animals, complete the first before the second.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action: Side I; enclosure state table

answers.answer: 1. Animals II permits playing animals from the display within reputation range as well as from hand; a display animal costs its folder number extra, and the display is not replenished until end of turn. 2. At strength 5 or more, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action so the increased range applies to animals played that action. 3. Animals II also permits animals with an upgrade-required condition.

1. Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you relocate all corresponding eligible animals that fit, choosing separately for each animal; each must meet the new building's terrain adjacency and capacity requirements. 2. Mark each relocated animal's required special-enclosure capacity with that many supply player tokens. 3. For each animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all of its requirements including terrain. If none does, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets its size requirement; if none meets even size, flip none. 4. This is relocation, not Release into the Wild, and applies to construction through permitted bonuses too.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure

answers.answer: 1. The four Association task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4 and conservation project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task and requires at least 1 active worker; Association II performs one or more different tasks whose total task value is no greater than action strength, using 1 or 2 workers per task as required. 3. If one of your workers is already on a task, repeating it requires placing 2 workers; if 3 of your workers are already there, you cannot do it again until after a break. 4. Other players' workers on a task do not matter.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action: Side I and The tasks; Side II

answers.answer: 1. Take partner zoos and universities from available tiles on the Association board and put them on the lowest empty relevant space on your zoo map; take the printed covered-space bonus immediately. For a university, also resolve its own reputation award immediately. 2. You cannot take a duplicate university; partner zoos must be from different continents and you can have at most four. The third or fourth partner zoo requires Association II. 3. A partner zoo gives its continent icon and discounts animal costs from that continent by 3 money per matching continent icon. 4. The hand-limit university raises the break hand limit from 3 to 5; the other universities do not change it.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action: Gain partner zoo; Gain university; University tiles

answers.answer: 1. A Conservation Project may be played from hand and supported immediately through Association I; with Association II it may instead be played from a display folder within reputation range, paying that folder number, with no refill until end of turn. 2. To support, fulfill a printed condition, choose an unoccupied reward level, and place a token from the left edge of your zoo map on that condition; normally support a given project only once, and a level is blocked by any player's token. Gain the reward, then take the newly uncovered map bonus immediately, before or after the project reward as chosen. 3. New projects enter the leftmost space above the Association board and push existing ones right. If this exceeds the player-count capacity, discard the rightmost card and return its support tokens to their owners' supplies; map bonuses stay activated. 4. Base projects below the board do not move or replenish.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action: Conservation project work; Support procedure; Overflow

answers.answer: 1. Release projects use the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement as a category, not an exact-size match: 2− accepts size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5; the animal must also match the required category. Actual tile size or special-enclosure capacity is irrelevant to that category. 2. First subtract only the animal's printed appeal and remove/discard it and its icons; keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. 3. Playing a new Release project grants 1 reputation; supporting an existing one does not. 4. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its required tokens can be removed, remove them; only otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or the smallest meeting size alone if none meets all requirements, or none if no occupied enclosure meets size. Flock animals follow this too.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild projects work differently

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand if strength is at least its level and conditions are met; alternatively advance the Break token by strength and take that much money. 2. Sponsors II may play multiple Sponsors from hand and/or within-range display; strength plus 1 must be at least the sum of their levels, and each display card costs its folder number extra. Sponsors II also permits upgrade-conditioned cards. 3. Resolve cards one after another, fully resolving each card's instant effects before the next and delaying after-finishing effects until the action ends. 4. If choosing the money option on either side, take the full amount even if the Break token reaches its end early; Sponsors II pays the money twice (so twice the action strength).
answers.evidence: SPONSORS action: Side I and Side II

answers.answer: 1. Break steps in order: discard to hand limit (3, or 5 with hand-limit university); return Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock one tile of each partner-zoo continent/university kind except kinds already owned by everyone (no duplicates); discard display folders 1–2, slide remaining cards down and refill; take income; reset the Break token. 2. Kiosk income is 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify, while empty special enclosures do. 3. When multiple players take display cards during income, resolve them clockwise starting with the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them) and refill the display after each player before the next chooses. Other break income includes appeal money and break income from Sponsors and activated map bonuses.

1. At 2 conservation, choose either upgrade one Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or an available Bonus tile. The first time any player reaches 10, every player discards one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, all discard one before final scoring. 2. Check for game end at the end of your own turn or during a break when your appeal and conservation counters occupy the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn is checked by its owner at the end of their own turn or during a break. 3. After an own-turn trigger, the triggering player finishes and every other player takes one more turn; if triggered during a break, all players take one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card can add at most 4 conservation. Victory points equal appeal minus the lowest appeal value in the scoring area containing your conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; tie goes to the player with the most supported projects, then tied players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Conservation track; End of game; Final scoring

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the 9 Bonus tiles and place random face-up tiles on the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 conservation and two beside 8. Do not place tiles on the two yellow icon spaces; return the other five tiles to the box. 2. Physical component supply does not prohibit an otherwise legal play when a component runs out; use a suitable substitute. Explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability rules still apply.

1. Maps 1–8 are advanced maps on reverse sides, each with an individual ability; take 2 random zoo maps and choose 1 advanced map, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose one each in reverse turn order. 2. Map A begins with an empty size-3 standard enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; its printed kiosk is counted as built and a tile is placed over it as a reminder.

1. Each player puts 7 player tokens on the designated spaces at the left edge of their zoo map; these support conservation projects and uncover bonuses. 2. Hire inactive workers from the lowest reserve space upward. 3. Some maps grant conservation points when you hire your last worker.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2–C3; Association worker supply

answers.answer: 1. On earning an upgrade, flip one chosen Action card from side I to side II in its current slot. 2. Its improved action is usable starting with your next action, but it counts as upgraded immediately for conditions. 3. The ongoing action retains the strength and action kind set at its start; an upgrade during it does not grant side-II abilities during that action. 4. You cannot upgrade all five Action cards (one upgrade reward allows an alternative choice).
1. Cards I draws/discards at strengths 1–5+: 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1. 2. A required discard may be either a newly drawn card or one already in your hand.

1. The seven animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. Bears count as a category even when also shown with herbivore or predator; Petting Zoo animal is its own category. Include both unless the effect explicitly excludes them.
answers.evidence: Animal categories (7); Base glossary: shared principles

answers.answer: 1. Association II may make exactly 1 donation, but only after performing at least one Association task in that same action; donation needs no worker. 2. Pay the smallest money amount still visible in the donation area and cover that space using a player token from your supply to gain 1 conservation. Printed sequence is 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then repeatable 12. Skip spaces blocked at setup; once every space but the last is covered, each later donation costs 12 and places no further token.

1. Zoo icons include upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards; on Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards also count upper-left water/rock requirements; count partner-zoo continent and university research icons. 2. Do not count left-side play conditions or Conservation Project icons; a university's reputation award and hand-limit mark are benefits, not zoo icons. 3. A card counts its own icons for its effects; doubled icons count twice, including triggering matching effects twice. For effects asking different icon types, duplicates count as one type. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules.
answers.evidence: Counting icons in your zoo; shared principles

answers.answer: 1. For a requirement of two water or rock spaces, count distinct adjacent terrain hexes: multiple touching edges to one terrain hex count only once. A larger connected terrain area contributes only the hexes actually adjacent to the enclosure/building. 2. Connected terrain regions do not make nonadjacent hexes count, and water/rock illustrations on tiles are not terrain spaces or requirements.
answers.evidence: Counting icons in your zoo; Terrain adjacency

answers.answer: 1. Playing a new Release into the Wild Conservation Project grants 1 reputation to the player who plays it; later support of that project gives no such play bonus. 2. For all Breeding Program project cards 123–127, the requirement is the same at all three reward spaces on that card; if fulfilled, choose any available reward space.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild projects; ALL Breeding Program project cards

answers.answer: 1. For X:Y, X is the condition and Y the reward. 2. A condition without a number, or marked ‘per,’ pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; with multiple thresholds, use the highest one met.

1. A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. 2. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. ‘Your zoo’ includes your played cards, map and personal supply; ‘any zoo’ includes these for every player.

1. A unique building must be placed when its Sponsor is played; if it cannot legally be placed, the card cannot be played. 2. Use the matching tile with its colored face up; rotate freely but do not flip. Follow ordinary placement and its terrain requirements, with no size-based construction payment. 3. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals, and do not count as water or rock spaces.
answers.evidence: Unique buildings must be placed when playing their Sponsor

answers.answer: 1. For both a named Action and Determination (Any Action), finish the Animals action, including moving its card to slot 1, before taking the granted action. 2. Use the granted action's Action card normally, then move that card to slot 1 after the granted action. 3. A named Action must be performed as named and cannot be replaced by the X-token alternative; Determination lets you choose any action, including the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Action / Determination

answers.answer: 1. Assertion searches the unused face-down base-project deck and adds the chosen project to hand; Dominance searches for its named project and has no effect if that project is already in play. 2. Later play and immediately support the obtained project through Association, placing it above the Association board, not in the setup base-project row below it.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Assertion / Dominance

answers.answer: 1. Boost and Clever resolve after finishing Animals and moving that Action card. 2. Clever puts the chosen card in slot 1; cards formerly to its left shift right. Boost puts its named card in slot 1 or 5; if moved to 5, cards formerly to its right shift left.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Boost / Clever

answers.answer: 1. An affected zoo needs at least 5 appeal for Constriction, Hypnosis, Pilfering and Venom. Venom targets every other zoo with higher appeal; Constriction targets every other eligible zoo ahead on appeal and/or conservation; Hypnosis and Pilfering choose among highest-appeal eligible zoos (Pilfering 2 also separately considers most conservation). 2. The playing animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its interactive ability, so its new appeal normally need not count when choosing affected players. 3. The multiplayer group may use the alternative text marked for solo on these cards without playing solo mode.

1. A target ahead on one track gets one Constriction token on slot 5; one ahead on both tracks gets two, on slots 4 and 5. 2. Do not stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 3. Each affected action loses 2 strength, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. 4. Remove the token after acting or without effect at the next break.

1. At effective strength zero or below, a constricted card cannot be used as a regular action unless you spend enough X-tokens to reach at least strength 1. 2. Alternatively, take the X-token action or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3.

1. Digging 2 lets you choose up to twice between discarding one display card and replenishing it, or discarding a hand card then drawing one from the deck; you may choose differently after each card. 2. A display card discarded through Digging is replaced immediately, with higher folders shifted down and a new card drawn into folder 6.

1. A flock animal may avoid using a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least its standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore can host any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. 3. Without such a host, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot share its enclosure. 4. On release, no proof of historical residents is needed: release frees an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure even if the flock animal originally shared.

1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker, moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2. Take any conservation-point reward printed on your map for hiring your last worker. 3. If all workers are active, the ability has no effect.
1. Hunter reveals the specified number of deck cards, adds one revealed Animal card to hand and discards all other revealed cards. If none is an Animal, discard all of them.

1. Hypnosis selects a zoo tied for highest appeal among zoos with at least 5 appeal; if you select yourself it has no effect. Copy only a target card in slot 1, 2 or 3. 2. Use the targeted owner's upgraded or unupgraded side for that whole action, but use your own X-tokens and your own cards for other upgrade checks. 3. Apply Venom and Constriction on the copied card to you and discard those tokens afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. Move the copied card to slot 1 normally.

1. A Multiplier gained from a reward naming an Action card goes on that card; one from a Bonus tile may go on any of your Action cards, including Animals. 2. On its next use, you may execute that action twice in succession at the same base strength, moving the Action card only after both. Each X-token boosts only one execution. 3. Defer after-finishing effects until both executions finish; a break triggered during the first waits until the whole turn is finished. 4. Return used Multiplier tokens to supply; remove unused ones at the next break.

1. Each additional Multiplier token adds one execution: two tokens permit up to three actions, not four. 2. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but you cannot mix an X-token action with a regular action. Different permitted options may be chosen in each regular execution.

1. Peacocking permits placing a Large Bird Aviary before Build II, provided your zoo does not already have one and there is a legal site; other restrictions still apply, including Build II for restricted-icon spaces. 2. Posturing follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing, and multiple buildings are placed one at a time.
1. The first Petting Zoo animal gives 3 appeal, the second 6 and the third 9. 2. The single Petting Zoo holds at most three such animals. 3. Petting Zoo animals count as small animals.

1. Pilfering 1 targets a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal; choose among ties. 2. Pilfering 2 separately resolves a highest-appeal target and the most-conservation target, each requiring at least 5 appeal; the conservation leader must have at least 1 conservation. 3. If all players have zero conservation, its conservation-target part has no effect, while its separate highest-appeal part still resolves normally. 4. A self-target has no effect; if the same zoo qualifies for both Pilfering 2 targets, it is targeted twice.

1. The target chooses to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. With no hand cards, target gives 5 money; with less than 5 money, target gives a card. With neither a card nor 5 money, target gives all current money, including zero. 3. Resolve repeated pilferings sequentially, and the target may choose differently each time.

1. Pouch tucks hand cards beneath the animal for 2 appeal per card; tucked cards have no remaining function. If the animal is released, discard its tucked cards too, but retain the appeal already earned. 2. Sunbathing sells up to the stated number of hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.

1. An extra Final Scoring card drawn through Resistance before the 10-conservation milestone joins the cards from which you choose one to discard at that milestone. 2. At game end score every remaining Final Scoring card, each subject to its own cap of at most 4 conservation points.

1. Shuffle the discard pile face down, draw the stated number of cards randomly, make the ability's stated selection, then return the discard pile face up. For the illustrated Scavenging 3, draw 3, keep 1 and discard the other 2.

1. Snapping takes exactly one card from the display regardless of reputation; drawing from the deck is not an alternative. 2. Sponsor Magnet takes display Sponsors without requiring them to be in reputation range; if no Sponsor is present, it has no effect. 3. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.

1. Venom places its X tokens on the lowest slots, starting at slot 1, at most one token per card; return duplicates to supply. 2. Using a marked card removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn, including use of the X-token alternative if you hold fewer than five X-tokens. 3. At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token that turn and at least one remains on your cards. If unable to pay, undo the turn and choose another action; spending all money cannot avoid the fee. 4. Unused tokens expire at the next break.

1. Veterinarian gives an immediate 2/5/10 money for 1/2/3 universities. 2. It changes the strength required to support a conservation project to 4 rather than 5. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation for three universities.
1. Medical Breakthrough gives 2 appeal for each previously supported project, counted by player tokens missing from the left edge of your zoo map. 2. It gives 1 conservation at each break.

1. Basic Research counts different continent and animal-category icon types together, excluding research; duplicates and doubled copies still count as one type. Gain 1 conservation per 2 types, rounding down. 2. Every other player gains 2 money per conservation point you gain.

1. Science Library gives 1 appeal per research icon when played. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, its owner gains 2 money. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation with five different animal categories.

1. Expert on the Americas gives 1 appeal per Americas icon immediately. 2. Each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk, following ordinary placement and kiosk-spacing rules. 3. Its final condition is five or more kiosks for 1 conservation.

1. Expert on Australia gives 1 appeal per Australia icon immediately. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card beneath this Sponsor for 2 appeal; tucked cards have no further function.

1. When playing either Global Breeding Program or Breeding Program, take 2 player tokens from your supply and place them on that Sponsor's two printed spaces. 2. When supporting a base project below the Association board, you may return exactly 1 of those tokens to your supply as one icon; you may not spend both on the same project. Base-origin cards later played above the board do not qualify. 3. Final reward: 1 conservation with five or more project supports, counted by missing left-map tokens.

1. Engineer permits one extra copy of a building built in that same Build action without extra strength, but you pay its normal money cost and follow placement rules. 2. Only one extra building is allowed even if you build several different kinds; special enclosures still have a one-per-type limit. 3. Its final reward is 5 appeal with the map full except water/rock.

1. Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon immediately. 2. It lets you cover water/rock spaces and ignore animal and unique-building terrain requirements; printed terrain icons still count, and terrain need not be covered for full-map scoring. 3. Covered terrain no longer counts for Hydrologist, Geologist or Architectural Zoo. 4. It scores 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, maximum three pairs.

1. Archaeologist triggers when an actual placement bonus on a border space is gained. 2. For each such bonus, choose any uncovered placement bonus on your map, not necessarily on a border; multiple triggers may choose the same or different bonuses. Resolve them in chosen order. 3. Final condition: all building border spaces covered, excluding water/rock, for 1 conservation.

1. Migration Recording gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gives 1 additional conservation. You may repeatedly support the same release project using different qualifying animals, but place at most one token on that project per Association action. 3. Each such token counts as a separate project support for other effects.

1. Quarantine Lab gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering; against Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and identify the next qualifying player. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation with all five continents.

1. WAZA Special Assignment permanently chooses small or large, marks that box with a supply player token, and reveals deck cards until finding an animal of that type; keep it and discard the others. 2. You cannot play the opposite type. 3. Chosen small animals get 2 extra appeal, chosen large animals get 4; size-3 animals remain legal but get no bonus.

1. WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal immediately. 2. If an Animals action contains only small animals, you may play one additional small animal from hand with normal costs/rules. 3. Then add one small animal from the display to hand regardless of reputation; you may take it even if you declined the extra play. Mixing small and large animals in the original action prevents this effect.

1. Hydrologist gives 1 appeal per water icon when played. 2. Each newly covered space adjacent to water gives 1 money, even if several spaces belong to one building; a space adjacent to multiple water hexes pays only once. 3. Its final condition is all water hexes connected (none isolated), for 1 conservation.
1. Barred Owl Hut places its unique building. 2. Each bird icon played triggers drawing 2 deck cards, keeping 1 and discarding the other.
1. Sea Turtle Tank's unique building must be placed adjacent to water. 2. Each reptile icon played permits selling up to 2 hand cards for 4 money each; discard the sold cards.

1. Each predator icon played triggers Hunter with a number of draws equal to your total predator icons. 2. A new card with two predator icons triggers two sequential Hunters, counting both new icons each time.

1. Okapi Stable is placed with 3 supply tokens on its card. 2. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to a hand Sponsor's level to play that Sponsor, meeting normal conditions. 3. The Stable's own herbivore icon can trigger this on its play; it allows three total uses and the Sponsor must come from hand.

1. Zoo School gives 1 reputation and 1 conservation. 2. Place its unique building covering at least two border spaces. 3. Take one display card within reputation range or draw one deck card; resolve simultaneous benefits in any order you choose.

1. Side Entrance's unique building occupies two border spaces and need not touch an existing building; other placement rules apply, and later buildings may attach to it. 2. At each break it gives 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may stand beside a kiosk. 3. As a unique building it counts as an adjacent building for kiosk income. 4. Its final reward is 5 appeal with a full map excluding water/rock.

1. Native Farm Animals gives 1 appeal per connected uncovered building border space; water and rock are never included. 2. At end game it gives 1 conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluating each group separately. 3. Upgrade-restricted spaces count even if Build was not upgraded; water/rock spaces do not count.

1. Explorer gives 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon; research icons do not count. 2. Each category/continent newly introduced to your zoo gives 1 appeal and 2 money. A newly played double of the same new icon grants the novelty benefit only once.

1. WAZA Large Animal Program lets you place a size-5 standard enclosure free under normal placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, ignore one left-side condition (such as one required icon or Animals upgrade); terrain requirements cannot be ignored. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, allowing two conditions to be ignored.

1. Biodiverse Zoo compares your number of icons in each animal category with the player to your right and gives 1 conservation for each category in which you have more. 2. If that player has none of a category, one of your icons is enough to exceed them. 3. Maximum reward is 4 conservation.

1. Observation Tower benefits only standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not merely another rock hex. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify, and the tower is not a building for kiosk income. 3. Housing an animal in a qualifying standard enclosure gives the two appeal again even if an earlier animal was released from it.

1. Outdoor Areas applies to standard enclosures touching the Outdoor Area hex itself, not merely another water hex. 2. Such an enclosure counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement (so physical size 2 is treated as size 4). 3. You cannot ignore this for release or transfer. 4. It does not affect special enclosures, and Outdoor Area is not a building.

1. A building on the Commercial Harbor's adjacent building space activates it; your first building may start there but need not. 2. Its discard ability can be used before, during or after your action, once per own turn, never during a break or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.

1. Park Restaurant income is 1 money per adjacent covered hex, regardless of building type, occupancy or how many belong to the same building; empty enclosures qualify. 2. The Restaurant itself is not a building. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus gives one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; choose one, not both, and follow other normal placement rules.

1. Cover Hollywood Hills H spaces by placing buildings under ordinary placement rules. Each covered H reveals deck cards until a Sponsor appears; keep that Sponsor and discard the others. 2. H spaces are not placement bonuses and do not trigger Archaeologist. 3. After all three H spaces are covered, every Sponsor's level is one lower. 4. Bonus partner zoos still require Association II for the third/fourth partner; bonus buildings still require Build II for restricted-icon spaces.

1. Pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet its usual conditions. 2. The bonus permits playing the Sponsor only from hand, even with Sponsors II; it does not permit a display card. 3. The Sponsors Action card stays in its current slot and does not move.

answers.answer: 1. Venom affects every other zoo with higher appeal than yours and at least 5 appeal. 2. Hypnosis chooses a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal, among ties, and can copy only its slot 1, 2 or 3; self-target has no effect. 3. Pilfering 1 chooses among highest-appeal zoos with at least 5 appeal. Pilfering 2 separately chooses a highest-appeal and a most-conservation zoo, each with at least 5 appeal; the conservation leader needs at least 1 conservation. Ties are chooser's choice; self-target has no effect. 4. Constriction affects every other zoo with at least 5 appeal that is ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation; ahead on one track gets 1 token (slot 5), ahead on both gets 2 (slots 4 and 5).

An Animal-card partner-zoo condition requires a partner zoo from that animal's continent; a Sponsor-card partner-zoo condition may be satisfied by a partner zoo from any continent. 2. A left-side maximum-25-appeal condition permits play only while you have at most 25 appeal; its marker at 25 is only a reminder, not a general track cap. 3.
